newsitem.title: UK: UK rail watchdog to act over inquiry lines -paper.
newsitem.headline: UK rail watchdog to act over inquiry lines -paper.

text.p: Britain's recently privatised train operating companies could face draconian fines for failing to provide an adequate national rail inquiry service, the Guardian newspaper said on Tuesday.
The paper said rail regulator John Swift is to issue an ultimatum to the industry warning it to improve its telephone inquiry service within two weeks or face fines of several million pounds.

It said such action would hit the share prices of companies such as Stagecoach Holdings Plc, Sea Containers Ltd and National Express Group Plc. The paper said rail customers had complained about the deteriorating service on information lines.

Under the watchdog's guidelines, the inquiry service -- which gives passengers details of train times and connections -- is supposed to answer 90 percent of all calls and 95 percent of these within 30 seconds, it said.
But the firms are falling short of these targets and the situation is worsening, although not all have failed to provide a proper service, the paper added.
Penalties would be imposed on the Association of Train Operating Companies, which represents 25 firms.
